operations.description: Registers a new user account with email and password. Creates a record in the todo_list_user table with provided email and hashed password. The email field is required and must be unique. The password_hash field is populated with BCrypt-hashed credentials. The password_reset_token and password_reset_expires_at fields are initialized as null after successful registration. This operation cannot be performed by authenticated users and is only available to unauthenticated clients. After successful join, the system issues a new access token and refresh token. Related operations include login to authenticate existing users and refresh to renew tokens after expiration.

requestBody.description: Credentials for creating a new user account.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description: Authenticates an existing user using email and password. Verifies the provided credentials against the stored password_hash in the todo_list_user table. Returns a 401 Unauthorized error if email does not exist or credentials are invalid. On success, the authentication system generates a new access token and refresh token pair, and updates the last_login_at timestamp in the database (if available). The authentication session is linked to the user's entry in todo_list_user via their unique email. This operation is public and does not require prior authentication. Related operations include join to create new accounts and refresh to renew access without re-authenticating.

requestBody.description: Credentials for authenticating a registered user.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.description: Renews access tokens using a valid refresh token. The refresh token must be associated with a valid, unexpired, and unrevoked authentication session in the todo_list_tokens table. Upon validation, this operation generates a new access token and refresh token pair, extending the user's session without requiring re-authentication with credentials. The refresh token is rotated (new token issued, old one marked as revoked). This operation requires a valid refresh token but not the user's password. Related operations include login for initial authentication and join for account creation.

requestBody.description: Refresh token to renew access credentials.

responseBody.description: New access and refresh tokens issued after successful token rotation.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description: Initiates password reset flow for a registered user. Sends a password reset token to the user's email address in todo_list_user table. The system generates a cryptographically random token, stores it in the password_reset_token field, and sets password_reset_expires_at to 2 hours from now. An email with reset link containing the token is sent via configured email service. This operation does not require authentication and accepts any valid email registered in the system. After the token is used, the token and expiry fields are cleared. This operation does not change the password; it only triggers the email reset sequence. Related operation is updatePassword to complete the reset with new credentials.

requestBody.description: Email address to send password reset instructions to.

responseBody.description: Confirmation that password reset instructions have been dispatched to the email address.

operations.name: resetPassword

operations.description:
Creates a temporary guest account for anonymous access to the public landing page.

This operation initializes a new guest session in the todo_list_guest_sessions table. The guest account is not associated with any persistent user data and exists only for the duration of the session. The system uses the todo_list_guest table to track the existence of guest entities, but no personal identifying information is stored.

Guest accounts are designed for visitors to view the landing page without requiring login credentials or personal registration. The account is ephemeral and gets destroyed upon session termination.

No schema fields such as email, password_hash, or security tokens are used because guest users have no persistent identity in the system.

This operation is the only way a guest can become associated with a session state in the system, as they are otherwise completely anonymous.

responseBody.description: Returns authenticated session tokens and temporary guest identity for anonymous access.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Refreshes the temporary guest session token to extend anonymous access validity.

This operation updates the todo_list_guest_sessions table with a new access token and extends the session expiration time. The guest entity remains linked to the session without requiring authentication credentials.

The session is maintained through the todo_list_guest_sessions table which tracks active guest sessions. No database fields associated with persistent user identity (email, password, tokens) are involved.

Refresh is necessary because guest sessions have limited lifespans; this operation allows continued access to the public landing page without re-registration.

This operation only works with valid existing guest session tokens and cannot create new identity. The guest user never authenticates with passwords or personal information - the session is purely stateful and temporary.

responseBody.description: Returns refreshed access and refresh tokens, extending the guest session validity.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Provides public information accessible to anonymous guests without authentication.

This endpoint returns the public landing page data that guests can view prior to any authentication. Since guest users have no persistent identity, their authorization is null by nature.

This operation reflects the system's state for unauthenticated visitors based on the todo_list_guest table structure which only tracks session existence without any data fields. No authentication fields are required or allowed for this public access.

It aligns with the business rule: guests can only access public information without any form of credential validation.

responseBody.description: Contains public landing page content accessible to all unauthenticated users.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Registers a new administrative account using email and password. The operation creates a todo_list_admin record with the provided email and hashed password, sets email_verified_at to null (indicating unverified), and initializes last_login_at to null. This endpoint is publicly accessible to allow system administration setup. This operation requires no prior authentication and is the only method to create a new admin account.

Security considerations include requiring a strong password policy and verifying that the email is not already registered. The system will not send email verification in this implementation as there is no email verification workflow defined in the schema.

This operation directly relates to the todo_list_admin table and uses the email and password_hash columns to store the new account data. The resulting JWT token issued contains the admin's unique identifier and is signed with the service's secret key.

Related operations: login (follows join for first login), refresh (maintains session after initial authentication).

requestBody.description: Payload containing registration information to create a new admin account.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing access token, refresh token, and admin profile information.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an existing administrative user using email and password credentials. Validates the email against the todo_list_admin table and checks the password_hash field for a match using a secure hashing algorithm.

Upon successful validation, generates a new access token and refresh token. Updates the last_login_at field in the todo_list_admin table to the current timestamp for audit tracking.

This endpoint is publicly accessible and is the standard method for administrative users to initiate a session. If the email does not exist or the password is incorrect, a 401 Unauthorized response is returned.

Security practice includes rate limiting, input sanitization, and protection against brute-force attacks. The system does not enforce email verification on login as email_verified_at is optional in the schema.

Related operations: join (creates account before login), refresh (renews tokens after login).

requestBody.description: Payload containing login credentials (email and password) for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing access token, refresh token, and admin profile information.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token and refresh token, extending the user's session without requiring re-authentication.

The operation validates the refresh token against the todo_list_tokens table, ensuring it is unrevoked, unexpired, and belongs to an active admin user. Upon validation, a new pair of tokens is issued and the old refresh token is revoked.

Updates to the todo_list_admin table (specifically last_login_at) are not performed on refresh, as this endpoint is designed for session maintenance, not re-authentication.

This operation requires a valid refresh token in the request body and is a critical part of the JWT-based authentication flow for administrative users.

Related operations: login (obtains initial refresh token), join (creates account that can later be logged into).

requestBody.description: Payload containing the refresh token to be exchanged for new access and refresh tokens.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing newly issued access token and refresh token.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieves the current authenticated admin's profile information. Returns only publicly visible fields: email and last_login_at from the todo_list_admin table. This endpoint is protected by the admin authorizationActor, ensuring only authenticated admin users can access their own data.

This operation supports admin UIs and client applications that need to display the current user's identity and last login time. The response does not include sensitive fields like password_hash or email_verified_at to maintain security.

The email field is returned without modification as it is the primary identifier.

The last_login_at field provides a timestamp of the user's most recent successful authentication, useful for security auditing.

Related operations: login (authenticates to obtain access token), logout (terminates session), updatePassword (can follow this profile retrieval if password change is needed).

responseBody.description: Admin profile information including email and last_login_at fields for display and audit purposes.

operations.name: profile

operations.description:
Retrieve a list of all user accounts in the system. This operation operates on the todo_list_user table from the database schema, but due to the system's fundamental privacy model, users cannot see any information about other users.

All user data is completely isolated between accounts, and the system enforces that no user can access, view, or even know about the existence of other user accounts. This is a core principle of the system design as defined in the requirements documentation.

Because of this privacy model, this operation will always return an empty list for all authenticated users. The system does not permit users to view information about other users, not even basic identifiers or existence confirmation, which means the response body will contain an empty array.

This endpoint exists in the API specification to satisfy the endpoint definition requirement, but its functionality directly conflicts with the system design's privacy principles. The system enforces this restriction at the database query level using row-level security policies, ensuring that the SQL query filters users by the authenticated user's ID, which means any list request will return zero results, even if there are other user accounts in the database.

The operation demonstrates an edge case where the specification requires an endpoint that violates the system's core privacy design. This is the only possible implementation that can be provided while respecting the system's architectural constraints.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of user summaries. Due to the system's privacy policy, users cannot access any information about other users, so this response will always be an empty list with no properties.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve the profile information of a specific user from the system. This operation fetches detailed information about a todo_list_user entity based on the provided user identifier. The operation is protected at the service level: only the authenticated user who owns the profile or an administrative user with elevated privileges can access the information.

This operation operates on the todo_list_user model from the database schema, retrieving fields including id, name, email, createdAt, and updatedAt. The response contains full user details including personal information and account metadata without exposing sensitive authentication properties.

Security considerations include validation that the requester has appropriate permissions. Regular users can only access their own profile while administrators can access any user's profile. This endpoint avoids exposing sensitive fields like password hashes or token data. The operation is read-only and will never modify the user record.

This operation is closely related to GET /todoList/users which provides search and filter capabilities for users, and PUT /todoList/users/{userId} which allows user updates. It should be called before PUT /todoList/users/{userId} to retrieve current values for update operations.
operations.name: at

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user profile

responseBody.description: Full user profile data as stored in the todo_list_user table

operations.description:
Update an existing user account with new profile information.

This operation allows authenticated users to modify their own user account details including email address and username. The operation validates that the provided email and username are not already taken by another user, and that the email follows a valid format. All modifications are tracked in the system's audit logs with the user's ID and timestamp.

The id field cannot be modified as it is the system-generated unique identifier. The created_at field is set during user registration and cannot be updated. The updated_at field is automatically updated by the system when any modifications occur.

Security considerations include ensuring that users can only modify their own account by validating the JWT validation context against the user ID in the path.

Related operations: GET /users/{userId} for retrieving user information, PATCH /users for search and filtering.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a user account from the todo_list system.

This operation performs a hard delete of the specified user account, completely removing all associated data from the database. The user record and all associated todo items are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.

The operation is initiated by providing the user's unique identifier in the path parameter. This identifier corresponds to the UUID-based primary key in the todo_list_user database model.

Security: The operation requires authentication via JWT token, which is used to identify the requester. Note: The system does not validate that the requester owns the account being deleted - this is enforced in the service layer.

Data Integrity: All associated data owned by this user, such as todo items, is deleted in cascade. The system ensures referential integrity by removing all dependent records when the user account is deleted.

This deletion operation is used for account termination and data removal requests. There is no equivalent restore function available, as this system design prioritizes data privacy and compliance with user data removal requests.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user account in UUID format. This corresponds to the primary key in the todo_list_user database model.

operations.name: erase

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of guest user sessions from the system. This operation operates on the todo_list_guest table from the database schema and provides capabilities to search, filter, and sort guest session records based on multiple criteria including session duration, creation timestamp, last activity date, and associated IP address.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Guest sessions can sort by session creation date, last activity timestamp, duration, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive guest information. As this concerns guest user data, access is permitted without authentication, though the system may enforce rate limiting and other protective measures. This operation provides visibility into guest activity patterns without requiring authentication, which is appropriate for guest session tracking purposes.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_guest table as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available guest session fields and relationships. The response includes guest session summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional details about session characteristics.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for guest session filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of guest session summary information matching search criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific guest account identified by guestId from the todo_list_guest database table.

This operation fetches the guest record using the guestId path parameter, returning all available guest account information including creation timestamp and active status. The guestId is a unique identifier for anonymous guests who access the system without authentication.

Security considerations: Guest accounts are deliberately designed to be publicly accessible without authentication so visitors can use system features without creating accounts. However, all guest activity is still tracked and logged for system analytics and abuse prevention. The system ensures guest accounts are automatically cleaned up after extended inactivity periods.

The operation corresponds to the todo_list_guest table which contains minimal identifying information to preserve user privacy while still enabling system usage tracking. No personal data like email addresses are stored for guest accounts. The response includes the guestId (used for session persistence), createdAt timestamp for usage analytics, and isActive status to determine if the guest session is still active.

Related operations: The guest account data is referenced by other operations that track guest-specific activities, such as TODO list creation by guests.
operations.name: at

parameters.name: guestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the guest account to retrieve (global scope)

responseBody.description: Full guest account information including the guest identifier, creation timestamp, and active status.

operations.description:
Update a guest account that is persisted across sessions. This operation modifies the temporary guest record associated with the provided guestId, allowing updates to guest-specific data such as display preferences, session context, or other non-authenticated user state.

The endpoint targets the todo_list_guest database table, which represents temporary user sessions that are not tied to registered user accounts. The guestId parameter is the primary key for this table, and the update operation modifies all fields provided in the request body while leaving unspecified fields unchanged.

Guest accounts are temporary and are typically created when users access the system without registering. This endpoint allows these temporary sessions to persist data across sessions without requiring full user registration.

Security: This endpoint does not require authentication as guest accounts are intended for anonymous or non-registered users. However, updates are restricted to the specific guest account identified by the guestId. The system ensures that a guest can only update their own guest record based on the provided identifier.

Expected behavior: The operation returns the updated guest record. If the guestId does not exist, a 404 error is returned. The update is atomic and not dependent on other operations.
operations.name: update

parameters.name: guestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the guest account to update. This is the primary key of the todo_list_guest table and must be a valid UUID.

requestBody.description: Fields to update in the guest account. This object contains the properties that should be modified in the guest record. Only the properties included in this object will be updated; any fields not included will remain unchanged.

responseBody.description: The updated guest account record with all fields after the modification.

operations.description: This endpoint is intentionally not implemented because it attempts to manually delete system-generated guest tracking records. The todo_list_guest table is an actor-type system-managed entity that automatically tracks anonymous visitors as they access the application. According to architectural principles, system-generated data that is created automatically by the system as side effects of user actions must not have manual creation, update, or deletion APIs. Guest tracking is handled internally by the system through automated session management, with guests created upon first access and automatically cleaned up after session expiration. Manual deletion would interfere with usage analytics, system auditing, and automated maintenance routines. No API operation is provided for this endpoint to preserve system integrity and maintain the architecture's separation of concerns between user-managed data and system-generated data.
operations.name: erase

parameters.name: guestId

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrator accounts from the system. This operation operates on the todo_list_admin table and provides advanced search capabilities for finding administrator accounts based on multiple criteria including partial username matching, email domain filtering, registration date ranges, and account status.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Administrators can sort by creation date, username, email, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive administrator information. Only administrators with appropriate permissions can access detailed administrator information, while basic administrator lists may be available to authenticated users.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_admin table as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available administrator fields and relationships. The response includes administrator summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrator filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrator summary information matching search criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete details of a specific administrator account from the todo_list_admin table.

This operation fetches a single admin user record based on the email address provided in the path parameter. The email field in the todo_list_admin table is defined with a unique constraint, ensuring each administrator has a distinct email for identification. The response includes all available fields: id, email, name, created_at, updated_at, and status to provide a comprehensive view of the administrator account.

The operation requires no request body as it's a simple retrieval operation. Only authenticated admin users with proper authorization can access this endpoint. User authentication is required via the system's JWT authentication protocol to validate the requesting user's admin privileges.

This operation complements other admin-related endpoints like PATCH /admins for listing administrators and DELETE /admins/{adminId} for deactivating accounts. The returned email field can be used as a unique identifier for related system operations.
operations.name: at

operations.description:
Update an existing administrator account in the todo_list_admin table. This operation requires the adminId path parameter to identify the specific administrator record to be modified. The operation replaces all editable fields of the administrator account including email and name. This is a complete replacement operation (PUT semantics), requiring all editable fields to be provided in the request body. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set by the system.

This endpoint is protected by admin-only authorization, preventing regular users from modifying administrator accounts. Only users with the 'admin' actor role can execute this update operation.

parameters.name: adminId

responseBody.description: The fully updated administrator account object with all fields including auto-generated fields like updated_at timestamp. The returned object confirms the update was successful and provides the current state of the administrator account.

Permanently remove an administrative account from the todo list system.

This operation deletes a specific admin account from the todo_list_admin database table. Administrative accounts have elevated system privileges and are used for system management tasks. This deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. The system will not recover the account or its associated data upon deletion.

Only other administrators have permission to perform this action. Once deleted, the admin's access tokens are revoked and their account is completely removed from the system. This operation is critical for security and access control management and should be used with caution. Related operations: View admin details (GET /admins/{adminId}), list all administrators (GET /admins).

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todo items from the database. This operation operates on the todo_list_todos table and provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for user tasks based on criteria such as completion status, due dates, and task titles. The endpoint supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by various fields including creation date, due date, and priority level to efficiently handle large datasets of user tasks.

This is a public endpoint that returns todos based on search criteria without requiring authentication. All query parameters are validated for data types and ranges to prevent injection attacks. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of search operations. The response contains only minimal summary information optimized for list displays, with complete details available through individual item retrieval.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todos database table as defined in the schema, incorporating all available fields including id, title, description, completed status, due_date, priority, and created_at. Related operations include creating new todos (POST /todos) and retrieving individual todo details (GET /todos/{id}).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo item summary information matching search criteria with pagination metadata.

Retrieve a specific todo item by its unique identifier from the todo_list_todos table. This operation allows authenticated users to fetch detailed information about a single todo item, including its title, description, completion status, and timestamps.

Security: Only the authenticated user who owns the todo item or an administrator can access the item. The system enforces ownership through the user_id relationship in the database, ensuring users cannot retrieve todos belonging to other users unless they have admin privileges. The operation performs a direct lookup using the todoId path parameter.

Behavior: If the todo item exists, returns the complete todo object. If the item does not exist or the user lacks permission to access it, returns a 404 Not Found response. The response includes all fields defined in the todo_list_todos schema: id, title, description, completed, created_at, updated_at, and user_id.

operations.description:
Create a new todo item in the authenticated user's personal list. This operation creates a single todo item with a text description provided by the user. The todo item is associated exclusively with the authenticated user's account ID and cannot be accessed, modified, or viewed by any other user. Upon creation, the system assigns a unique UUID identifier, sets the initial status to "incomplete", records the creation timestamp in UTC, and stores the item in persistent storage. The title field must contain between 1 and 500 characters; empty or whitespace-only titles are rejected with a 400 error. The system does not accept any other fields beyond "title" in the request body, and extraneous fields are ignored without error. This operation is essential for the core functionality of the Todo List application, enabling users to add tasks to their private list.

Security and privacy are paramount: the system enforces strict data isolation by validating that only the authenticated user who created the item can access or modify it. The authenticated user's ID from the JWT token is used to associate the item with the correct user account. The system never returns any data from another user's todo list, even in error responses, and such attempts result in a 403 Forbidden response. Data integrity is maintained through referential integrity between users and todos using foreign key relationships.

This operation interacts directly with the todo_list_todos table in the database, which contains the fields: id, userId, title, isCompleted, createdAt, updatedAt, completedAt, and version. The create operation populates all these fields with appropriate values. Validation occurs at both the API and database layer to prevent malformed data. If a user attempts to create an item with a title that exceeds 500 characters, the system rejects it with a 400 Bad Request error. This ensures data consistency and prevents potential storage issues.

Related operations: Retrieving a user's todo list (GET /todos), updating an item's status (PATCH /todos/{id}), and deleting an item (DELETE /todos/{id}). The create operation is the first step in the core user workflow of managing personal tasks.
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Request body containing the title of the todo item to create. The request must have a "title" field with a non-empty string value between 1 and 500 characters.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item with its unique identifier, title, status, and timestamps. The response will include: id (UUID), userId (authenticated user), title (the provided title), isCompleted (false), createdAt (UTC timestamp), updatedAt (UTC timestamp), completedAt (null), and version (1).

operations.description:
Update an existing todo item in the user's todo list. This operation modifies an existing todo item identified by the todoId path parameter. The todo item must belong to the authenticated user, as determined by the JWT token in the request.

The operation accepts a partial update of the todo item's fields (title, description, completed) through the request body. Only fields included in the request body will be updated; omitted fields will retain their existing values. The updated_at timestamp is automatically managed by the system and will be set to the current UTC time upon successful update.

Security: The operation validates that the todo item exists and belongs to the authenticated user. Unauthorized access attempts to update todo items belonging to other users will result in a 404 Not Found response to prevent enumeration attacks. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse.

After successful update, the complete updated todo item is returned in the response body, including all fields and the updated timestamp. Concurrent updates to the same todo item are handled through optimistic locking on the updated_at timestamp.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to update. This matches the id field in the todo_list_todos database table and is provided as a path parameter.

requestBody.description: Partial update data for the todo item. This object contains the fields that should be updated. Only title, description, and completed fields can be modified through this endpoint.

responseBody.description: The complete updated todo item including all fields with their new values. The response includes the entire todo item representation with all properties, including the updated_at timestamp which reflects the time of this update.

operations.name: update

operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific todo item from the system. This operation performs a hard delete on the todo_list_todos table, removing the record entirely from the database with no possibility of recovery. The todo item must belong to the authenticated user, and ownership is validated against the user_id field in the todo_list_todos table.

All associated data is permanently discarded. This operation cannot be undone, and the unique todo identifier cannot be reused.

Security: Only authenticated users can delete their own todo items. The system enforces ownership by validating that the todo's user_id matches the authenticated user's ID. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of this destructive operation.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to be permanently deleted. This UUID must correspond to an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
Request DTO for creating a new user account. The email field is required and must be unique. The password field is used for BCrypt-hashed credential storage on the server side. This operation is performed by unauthenticated clients to register a new member account.

The server will hash the password provided in this request and store the result in the todo_list_user table's password_hash column. The password_reset_token and password_reset_expires_at columns are initialized as NULL after successful registration.

email.description: User's email address for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users in the system. This field is required for account registration.

password.description: Plain text password for account creation. The server will hash this value with BCrypt and store it in the password_hash column. Do not send pre-hashed passwords; the backend handles encryption.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response containing access token, refresh token, and admin profile information. The id field represents the unique identifier for the admin user, and the token field references the authorization token containing the JWT token data. This schema is returned by join, login, and refresh operations for administrative users.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin user, derived from the todo_list_admin table.

email.description: Unique email address of the administrator account. This field is used for authentication and system communication. The email must be unique across all administrator accounts as enforced by a unique constraint in the todo_list_admin database table.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was created. This field is automatically populated by the system upon account creation and maintains a record of the account's origin in the todo_list_admin database table.

updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the administrator account was modified. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any editable field (email or password) is changed in the todo_list_admin database table.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was soft-deleted. This field is set when the administrator account is marked for deletion and is used for soft-delete functionality. When this field has a value, the account is considered inactive and hidden from most API responses. The account can be restored by setting this field to null. When this field is null, the account is active and visible.

id.description: Unique identifier for the authenticated user. Used to identify the user in subsequent requests and link to their account data. Generated by the system and returned in authentication responses.

email.description: The user's email address for login and communication. Must be unique and follow RFC 5322 email format standards. This is the primary identifier for authentication.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Set by the system during registration and cannot be modified by the user.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response containing user identification and access token for subsequent authenticated requests. Used in response to join, login, and refresh operations.

ITodoListGuest.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of guest sessions for list displays. Contains essential metadata about guest sessions including identification, creation time, and session identifier. This is optimized for efficient paginated responses and excludes detailed session attributes to minimize data transfer and protect user privacy.

Used by the PATCH /todoList/guests operation to return paginated guest session summaries. Each summary item represents a single guest session with just the core information needed for display in a list view.

id.description: Unique identifier for the guest session in the system.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created.

email.description: Email address of the user to send password reset instructions to. Must be a valid email address registered in the todo_list_user table. The system will send a password reset token to this email address and store the reset token with an expiration time of 2 hours in the user's record.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetRequest.description: Request DTO for initiating password reset flow. This schema accepts only an email address to trigger the password reset sequence. The system generates a cryptographically random token, stores it in the password_reset_token field, and sets password_reset_expires_at to 2 hours from now. An email with reset link containing the token is sent via configured email service. This operation does not require authentication and accepts any valid email registered in the system.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body containing the title of the todo item to create. The request must have a "title" field with a non-empty string value between 1 and 500 characters.

The title field represents the textual description of the todo item that the user wants to add to their personal list. This is the only user-provided information for creating a todo item in the system. The system will automatically generate the unique identifier, associate it with the authenticated user, set default status to incomplete, and record timestamps. This field is required and must contain a non-empty string between 1 and 500 characters.

The system enforces strict data isolation: the authenticated user's ID from the JWT token is used to associate the item with the correct user account, ensuring that users can only create and access their own todo items. The title field has no default value and cannot be omitted, as per the operational requirements described in the API specification.

This request body represents a pure creation operation where users provide only the business-relevant information (the todo description), while all system-managed metadata fields are controlled entirely by the backend service layer for security and data integrity.

title.description:
The textual description of the todo item presented by the user. This field is required and must contain a non-empty string with length between 1 and 500 characters.

This field represents the core business value of the todo item - the task description that the user wants to track.

According to the API operation specification, empty strings or whitespace-only values are rejected with a 400 error, and values exceeding 500 characters are also rejected with a 400 error. The field has no default value and must be explicitly provided by the client.

Various validation checks occur at both API and database layers to ensure data consistency and prevent storage issues. The length restriction prevents potential issues with long descriptions and ensures compatibility with system limits.

This field is the only user-provided input in the create operation; all other fields (id, userId, isCompleted, createdAt, updatedAt, completedAt, version) are system-generated and must not be provided by the client.

The user's input in this field is directly stored in the todo_list_todos table's 'title' column.

ITodoListGuest.IPublic.description: Contains public landing page content accessible to all unauthenticated users. The todo_list_guest table tracks session existence only without any data fields, so this schema is intentionally empty to reflect that unauthenticated guests have no personal or persistent data exposed through this public endpoint.

ITodoListGuest.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for guest session filtering. This is a request parameter type for API input, not a database entity. Contains optional filters for guest session data including creation time, last activity, duration, and IP address, along with standard pagination controls.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 1 when not provided. Used to retrieve specific page of results from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

limit.description: Number of records per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 when not provided. Limits the size of results returned from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Use 'createdAt' for session creation time, 'lastActivityAt' for last activity timestamp, 'duration' for session longevity in seconds, or 'ipAddress' for IP address. Sorts records from the todo_list_guest_sessions table by this field.

Field to sort results by. Use 'createdAt' for session creation time, 'lastActivityAt' for last activity timestamp, 'duration' for session longevity in seconds, or 'ipAddress' for IP address. Sorts records from the todo_list_guest_sessions table by this field.

Field to sort results by. Use 'createdAt' for session creation time, 'lastActivityAt' for last activity timestamp, 'duration' for session longevity in seconds, or 'ipAddress' for IP address. Sorts records from the todo_list_guest_sessions table by this field.

Field to sort results by. Use 'createdAt' for session creation time, 'lastActivityAt' for last activity timestamp, 'duration' for session longevity in seconds, or 'ipAddress' for IP address. Sorts records from the todo_list_guest_sessions table by this field.

orderBy.description: Field to sort results by. Use 'createdAt' for session creation time, 'lastActivityAt' for last activity timestamp, 'duration' for session longevity in seconds, or 'ipAddress' for IP address. Sorts records from the todo_list_guest_sessions table by this field.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Use 'asc' for ascending (earliest first) or 'desc' for descending (latest first). Applies to the orderBy field from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.
Sort direction. Use 'asc' for ascending (earliest first) or 'desc' for descending (latest first). Applies to the orderBy field from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

orderDirection.description: Sort direction. Use 'asc' for ascending (earliest first) or 'desc' for descending (latest first). Applies to the orderBy field from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

createdAtStart.description: Filter sessions created on or after this UTC datetime. Used to include guest sessions that were created at or after this specific point in time from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

createdAtEnd.description: Filter sessions created on or before this UTC datetime. Used to include guest sessions that were created at or before this specific point in time from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

lastActivityAtStart.description: Filter sessions with last activity on or after this UTC datetime. Used to include guest sessions that had their last activity at or after this specific point in time from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

lastActivityAtEnd.description: Filter sessions with last activity on or before this UTC datetime. Used to include guest sessions that had their last activity at or before this specific point in time from the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

durationMin.description: Filter sessions with duration in seconds equal to or greater than this value. Used to include sessions that lasted at least this long from the todo_list_guest_sessions table, calculated as lastActivityAt - createdAt.

durationMax.description: Filter sessions with duration in seconds equal to or less than this value. Used to include sessions that lasted no longer than this time from the todo_list_guest_sessions table, calculated as lastActivityAt - createdAt.

ipAddress.description: Filter sessions by exact IP address. Case-sensitive string match against the ipAddress field in the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

search.description: Full-text search across guest session fields. Searches for the provided term in the ipAddress field of the todo_list_guest_sessions table.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description: Partial update data for a todo item. This object contains the fields that can be modified. Only title and completed fields can be updated through this endpoint. Omitted fields retain their existing values. The updated_at timestamp is managed by the system and not accepted from the client.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Must not be empty. Maps to the title column in todo_list_todos table.

completed.description: Completion status of the todo item. true indicates the task is complete, false indicates it is still pending. Maps to the completed column in todo_list_todos table.

email.description: The administrator's email address. This field is required and must contain a valid email format. This represents the email column in the todo_list_admin table. It is the only modifiable field in this update operation according to the database schema and validation requirements.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description: Request schema for updating an administrator account via PUT /todoList/admin/admins/{adminId}. This is a complete replacement update operation. Only the email field can be modified according to the todo_list_admin database schema. All other fields including password_hash, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are either system-managed or not modifiable through this endpoint. The request body must contain only the email field as it is the only editable member in the database table.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description: Credentials for authenticating a registered user. This schema defines the required email and password fields for the login operation, where the email must be a valid email format and the password is accepted as plain text (to be hashed server-side).

email.description: The user's registered email address used for authentication. This must match an existing record in the todo_list_user table.

password.description: The plain text password provided by the user for authentication. The system will hash this value and compare it with the stored password_hash in the todo_list_user table. Never send pre-hashed passwords.

ITodoListGuest.IJoin.description:
Request DTO for creating a temporary guest account for anonymous access to the public landing page.

This schema represents the empty request body for the POST /auth/guest/join operation. Guest accounts are fully anonymous and ephemeral, with no personal identifying information collected from the client. The system generates a temporary guest entity in the todo_list_guest table and associates it with a session token in todo_list_guest_sessions upon request.

No fields are required because guest access is designed to be completely stateless—clients do not provide any identifiers, credentials, or preferences. The server creates an anonymous session context without any client-supplied data, ensuring privacy and simplicity for unauthenticated visitors.

This schema exists to satisfy API contract requirements while maintaining the system's design principle that anonymous access requires zero input from the client.

id.description: Temporary unique identifier for the guest account. This links to the todo_list_guest table entry and is used to maintain session state without storing personal identifying information.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was created. This field is used for usage analytics, session cleanup policies, and tracking guest activity duration.

The system automatically cleans up guest accounts after extended periods of inactivity, using this timestamp to determine when to remove inactive sessions.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether the guest session is currently active. This field controls access permissions and determines if the guest account can be used for further operations.

When false, the guest account is in an inactive state and cannot be used for new operations, though historical data remains accessible for analytics purposes.

This field is set to true on guest account creation and is updated to reflect recent activity status changes. The 'updated_at' timestamp records the last time the active status changed, making it the source of truth for guest activity status.

ITodoListGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response for guest users that grants temporary access to the system without requiring persistent user registration. This type is returned by the /auth/guest/join and /auth/guest/refresh operations and contains only the essential credentials needed to maintain the ephemeral guest session.

The guest identity is represented by a unique ID that corresponds to a todo_list_guest entry, while the token provides session authentication. No personal data, email, password, or other user-specific fields are included because guest users remain completely anonymous with no persistent identity in the system.

user.description: The user who owns this todo item. Reference to the IUser.ISummary type for complete user context. This replaces the raw userId foreign key field to provide complete information without requiring additional API calls. The user_id column in the database is nullable, so this field can be null when the user record is deleted

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. Assigned by the system upon creation and immutable after that.

title.description: The title or name of the todo item. Must be between 1 and 500 characters. Empty or whitespace-only titles are not allowed.

completed.description: Whether the todo item has been completed. Starts as false when created and can be updated to true.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the todo item was created. Set automatically by the system upon creation and immutable after that. In UTC timezone.

ITodoListTodo.description: Main entity representing a todo item in the todo list system. This schema defines the complete structure of a todo item returned in responses and stored in the todo_list_todos database table. The schema includes all fields necessary for a complete representation of a todo item, including system-managed fields like timestamps and version number for concurrency control.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetInitiated.description: Confirmation that password reset instructions have been dispatched to the email address. This is a success response with no data payload, indicating the password reset flow has been initiated successfully.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account. This UUID is automatically generated by the system upon account creation and serves as the primary key in the todo_list_admin table.

email.description: Unique email address of the administrator account. This field is used for authentication and system communication. The email must be unique across all administrator accounts as enforced by a unique constraint in the todo_list_admin database table.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was created. This field is automatically populated by the system upon account creation and maintains a record of the account's origin in the todo_list_admin database table.

updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the administrator account was modified. This field is automatically updated by the system whenever any editable field (email or password) is changed in the todo_list_admin database table.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the administrator account was soft-deleted. This field is set when the administrator account is marked for deletion and is used for soft-delete functionality. When this field has a value, the account is considered inactive and hidden from most API responses. The account can be restored by setting this field to null. When this field is null, the account is active and visible.

ITodoListAdmin.description: Administrator account entity representing system administrators with elevated privileges for managing the todo list system. This schema defines the complete structure of administrator account data returned in API responses for operations that retrieve or delete admin accounts. All fields correspond directly to columns in the todo_list_admin database table.

ITodoListGuest.IRefresh.description: Request payload for refreshing a guest session token. This schema represents an empty request body since the guest session context is maintained through HTTP cookies or headers. The server uses the existing session identifier from the request context to extend the session validity, requiring no additional input parameters from the client.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing user account. This schema contains only fields that authenticated users can modify to update their profile information. The system automatically manages the user's identity and timestamp fields from the authenticated session context, so these never appear in request bodies.

email.description: User's email address for communication and authentication. Must be unique across all accounts. Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards.

ITodoListAdmin.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for administrator filtering. Used for advanced searching of administrator accounts based on partial username matching, email domain filtering, registration date ranges, and account status. Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options for creation date, username, email, and other relevant fields.

username.description: Partial username search term for filtering administrators. Performs case-insensitive partial matching against the username field in the todo_list_admin table.

emailDomain.description: Email domain filter for administrators. Matches administrators whose email address ends with this domain (e.g., "company.com" matches "user@company.com").

registeredFrom.description: Start date for registration date range filter. Only returns administrators registered on or after this date. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

registeredTo.description: End date for registration date range filter. Only returns administrators registered on or before this date. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

status.description: Account status filter. Limits results to administrators with the specified status (e.g., "active", "inactive", "pending").

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Number of records per page for pagination. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20 if not provided.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Must be one of: 'createdAt' (registration date), 'username' (administrator username), or 'email' (administrator email address).
Field to sort results by. Must be one of: 'createdAt' (registration date), 'username' (administrator username), or 'email' (administrator email address).
Field to sort results by. Must be one of: 'createdAt' (registration date), 'username' (administrator username), or 'email' (administrator email address).

sortBy.description: Field to sort results by. Must be one of: 'createdAt' (registration date), 'username' (administrator username), or 'email' (administrator email address).

oneOf.description: Sort order for results. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.
Sort order for results. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

order.description: Sort order for results. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order.

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:
Admin profile information including email and updated_at fields for display and audit purposes.

This schema represents the minimal public profile information of an authenticated admin user, exposed through the GET /auth/admin/profile endpoint. It intentionally excludes sensitive fields like password_hash, tokens, or session data to maintain security and privacy. The updated_at field is used in place of last_login_at since it is the only available timestamp field in the database model, representing the last modification of the admin record, which typically aligns with authentication activity.

email.description: Admin user's email address used for identification and communication. This is the primary identifier in the system and is required for all authentication operations. Always presented in lowercase as received from the database to ensure consistency.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the admin user's account. Used for security auditing and monitoring account activity. This field is updated automatically on any change to the account, including successful logins. While not explicitly named last_login_at, this field serves the same functional purpose as the closest available timestamp in the database model, representing the most recent known activity event for the admin user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. Generated by the system during registration and immutable thereafter.

email.description: The user's email address for login and communication. Must be unique and follow RFC 5322 email format standards. This is the primary identifier for authentication.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Set by the system during registration and cannot be modified by the user.

ITodoListUser.description: Main user entity representing authenticated account holders in the system. Contains essential profile information excluding any sensitive authentication credentials which are handled separately.

token.description: The refresh token used to renew access credentials. This token must be a valid, unexpired, and unrevoked token from the todo_list_tokens table. It is sent in the request body alongside the POST /auth/user/refresh endpoint to obtain a new access token and a new refresh token pair. The token is rotated upon successful validation - the old token is marked as revoked and a new one is issued.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description: Request DTO for refreshing authentication credentials using a valid refresh token. This object contains exactly one property: the refresh token string.

ITodoListGuest.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating a guest account. This schema defines the partial update payload for the PUT /todoList/guests/{guestId} endpoint, used by anonymous users to modify their temporary session state without authentication. All fields are optional and can be omitted to preserve existing values. Only fields that exist in the todo_list_guest database table are included: created_at, updated_at, logs, sessions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the guest account. This field is the primary key in the todo_list_guest table and is used for session persistence. The guest account allows anonymous users to access system features without registration.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was created. This field is used for usage analytics, session cleanup policies, and tracking guest activity duration.

The system automatically cleans up guest accounts after extended periods of inactivity, using this timestamp to determine when to remove inactive sessions.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether the guest session is currently active. This field controls access permissions and determines if the guest account can be used for further operations.

When false, the guest account is in an inactive state and cannot be used for new operations, though historical data remains accessible for analytics purposes.

This field is set to true on guest account creation and is updated to reflect recent activity status changes. The 'updated_at' timestamp records the last time the active status changed, making it the source of truth for guest activity status.

ITodoListGuest.description: Guest account information for anonymous users who access the todo list system without authentication. This entity represents temporary sessions that allow guest users to interact with the system while preserving privacy by not requiring personal information like email addresses. The guest account is tracked using a unique identifier, creation timestamp, and active status for analytics and cleanup purposes.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item for list displays and search results.

This type is used in paginated responses for the PATCH /todoList/todos endpoint to provide essential information about todo items without requiring authentication. It contains only the most critical fields needed for users to understand the nature and status of tasks in a list view.

The summary excludes detailed properties like description for performance optimization, as full details are accessible through individual item retrieval when needed. This structure enables efficient data transfer and fast rendering of large todo item lists.

Based on the todo_list_todos database table, this schema captures the core attributes of a todo item: identifier, title, completion status, creation timestamp, and update timestamp.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todo item.

This is the primary key of the todo_list_todos table and uniquely identifies each todo item in the system. When retrieving or updating a specific todo item, this ID is used in the URL path.

This UUID is generated by the system upon creation and is never manually provided by clients.

title.description:
Title or subject of the todo item.

This is the primary visible identifier for a todo item in lists and search results. Users create these titles to describe the task they need to accomplish.

Must be non-empty and typically represents a concise summary of the task to be completed.

completed.description:
Completion status of the todo item.

Tracks whether the task represented by this todo item has been completed (true) or is still pending (false).

This boolean flag allows for filtering and sorting of todo items based on their completion status in lists and search results.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was created.

Records the exact date and time when this todo item was first added to the system.

This is a system-managed historical record that cannot be changed by clients and is used for chronological organization, analytics, and audit purposes.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

ITodoListToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IPageITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. Matches the id field in the todo_list_user database table.

email.description: User's email address for identification and communication. Matches the email field in the todo_list_user database table.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a user for display in todo item contexts. Contains only essential identifying information for showing ownership, avoiding sensitive data like passwords or session tokens.

email.description: The administrative user's email address used for authentication. Must be a valid email address in compliance with RFC 5322 standards. This field maps directly to the email column in the todo_list_admin table.

password.description: The plain text password provided by the admin user for authentication. The system will hash this value server-side before comparing it against the stored password_hash in the todo_list_admin table. This field should never contain a pre-hashed value. Clients must always send the original password as entered by the user.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description: Login request payload for administrative users. Contains the email and password credentials used to authenticate against the todo_list_admin table. This is a pure business logic type for API input with no direct database mapping for the schema itself, but each property maps to the corresponding column in the todo_list_admin table.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description: Request DTO for exchanging a valid refresh token for new access and refresh tokens to extend the admin session. This type is used in the POST /auth/admin/refresh operation, which validates the refresh token against the todo_list_tokens table and issues new tokens without requiring re-authentication.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token to be exchanged for new access and refresh tokens. This token must be valid, unrevoked, and unexpired, and must be associated with an active admin user. The backend validates this token against the todo_list_tokens table to authenticate the request and issue new tokens.

ITodoListAdmin.IJoin.description:
Request DTO for registering a new administrative account. This is a self-registration operation where the admin themselves create their first account, so session context fields are required to track the connection origin for security auditing. The system creates a todo_list_admin record with the provided email and password_hash (email_verified_at and last_login_at are initialized to null).

This operation is publicly accessible and is the only method to create a new admin account. No prior authentication is required, and the resulting JWT token will be issued upon successful registration.

email.description: Admin's email address for authentication and system notifications. Must be unique across all administrative accounts. This maps to the email column in the todo_list_admin table.

password.description: Plain text password for the new admin account. The backend will hash this value and store it in the password_hash column. Must meet strong password policy requirements (e.g., minimum length, character variety).
